question.text: There are ten boys <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>10</mn></msub></math> and five girls <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>G</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>.</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mn>5</mn></msub></math>  in a class. Then the number of ways of forming a group consisting of three boys and three girls, if both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> together should not be the members of a group, is _____.

solution.text:
Given, total number of boys is 10 and total number of girls is 5

So total number of selections =C310·C35=1200

No. of selections in which B1 & B2 both are there in group =C18·C35=80

Required no. of selections =1200-80=1120
